root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: `c->u.xpack.nval <= sizeof(c->u.xpack.rmap) / sizeof(c->u.xpack.rmap[0])` before the `rmap` write loop.
root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `cram_xpack_decode_init()` enters the reverse-map write loop, the attacker-controlled xpack header count `c->u.xpack.nval` must not exceed the fixed `rmap[256]` capacity.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable code parses `c->u.xpack.nval` from the xpack header and immediately uses it as the loop bound for `c->u.xpack.rmap[i] = v` without first enforcing that the count fits the 256-entry destination array. The fixed code rejects oversized `nval` before any reverse-map write executes.

nodes.state: The boundary/overflow `c->u.xpack.rmap[i] = v` write executes with `i >= sizeof(c->u.xpack.rmap) / sizeof(c->u.xpack.rmap[0])`, so the sink store uses an out-of-range reverse-map index.

edges.relation: The same attacker-controlled `c->u.xpack.nval` checked at the root event remains the loop bound (`c->u.xpack.nval`) when the boundary/overflow `rmap` write executes.
